edges.effect_quant: Pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest the direction is more reliable than any single pooled magnitude.
edges.mechanism: Aflatoxin metabolites form DNA adducts, especially in hepatocytes, and synergize with chronic liver injury or hepatitis to accelerate carcinogenesis. That makes its link with Hepatocellular carcinoma biologically strong even when exposure measurement in cohorts is imperfect.
edges.summary: Pooled meta-analytic evidence link aflatoxin exposure to higher risk of hepatocellular carcinoma in populations with dietary exposure. The average effect is usually large rather than dramatic, so this edge is better read as a risk modifier than a stand-alone cause or cure.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
